_doc: BEHAVIOUR CONTRACTS — what a Velt control must still DO after you customize it. A pixel diff proves a control LOOKS right; nothing proved it still works, and the whole premise of primitives is that your markup keeps the SDK's behaviour. These are keyed to the PRIMITIVE FAMILY, never to a design: the SDK's behaviour is invariant across customizations, so one contract covers every build that places those primitives.
howItRuns: scripts/behaviour-check.mjs resolves which contracts apply from the primitives the PLAN places, then drives each against the live app and asserts an OBSERVABLE outcome. Selectors come from probe-selectors.json + the plan's own vcClasses, so nothing here hardcodes a design.
whyEachCarriesAMutation: A check that cannot fail is worse than no check — it reads as evidence. Every contract names a mutation that MUST trip it, so mutation-drill can score the suite's recall the same way it scores the visual detectors.

contracts.why: The input must render Velt's own contenteditable. If your markup replaced it, typing goes nowhere and every downstream composer behaviour is dead.
contracts.mutation: remove the contenteditable inside the composer input

contracts.why: composerTextChange is the published signal a customization reads to drive its own states. If it does not fire, every state a design keys on content is dead.
contracts.mutation: drop targetComposerElementId so the stream cannot be addressed

contracts.why: clearComposer is how a customized Cancel empties the field. If it no-ops the design's Cancel is decorative.
contracts.mutation: register the composer under a different targetComposerElementId

contracts.why: The headline promise of a composed composer. A silent no-op is indistinguishable from success without counting the collection before and after — which is why this is measured, not eyeballed.
contracts.mutation: point submitComment at an unknown composer id

contracts.why: A control that renders but is not the top element at its own centre is unclickable — a transparent overlay, a zero-size host, a sibling stealing the point. It looks perfect and does nothing, and this is the cheapest way to catch it.
contracts.mutation: cover a control with a transparent overlay

contracts.why: The trigger owns the click. A chip composed from the leaves alone renders pixel-perfect and never opens anything — the dead-compound-trigger class. SCOPED: only runs when the phase's design actually draws the OPEN menu — a closed dropdown is the correct resting state, not a defect.
contracts.mutation: place the trigger's leaves without the trigger ancestor

scoping: A contract runs only if the phase DRAWS the state it exercises. requiresDrawnState names that state; if no block in blocks.json covers it, the contract is skipped, not failed. Without this the suite reports later phases' work as this phase's defects.
